A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a definitive histopathological diagnosis of Castleman disease can be achieved with the use of immunohistochemistry, as a gold-standard for definitive diagnosis of Castleman Disease.

the histomorphologic and immunohistochemical features of a lymph node are the most important tools for accurate diagnosis, and that the use of ancillary techniques is essential in cases of diagnostic uncertainty.
the histopathological features of CD are not pathognomonic and may mimic other lymphoproliferation disorders.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a definitive diagnosis of Castleman disease is possible only with the use of immunohistochemistry, as a gold diagnostic tool, and not with the use of routine histopathology alone, especially in the presence of systemic manifestations.
the immunohistochemical panel should be extended to include CD3, CD4, CD8, CD10, BCL2, BCL6, CD30, CD138, CD20, CD79a, and Ki67, in addition to the routine panel (H&E stain and CD45).
immunohistochemistry can help in distinguishing between the different types of Castleman disease and lymphoma, which can have similar histological appearances.
